newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel rises against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel rises against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed higher against the dollar on Thursday following the decline of the U.S. currency in Europe, dealers said.

"Since the beginning of the week the Bank of Israel had to buy almost $500 million to support the basket. Today the central bank remained out of the market and we saw demand for dollars for the first time (this week) from the business sector," said a dealer at United Mizrahi Bank.
The central bank has been intervening regularly in the market to defend the foreign currency basket rate, which has been trading at the bottom end of its band for two months.
"Investors used the opportunity of the U.S. currency's decline abroad to buy dollars. They also bought dollars because there will be no trading on Monday due to the Jewish holiday of Purim," he said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3600 shekels against 3.3650 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6552 shekels against 3.6541 on Wednesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7416 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.7323 on Wednesday, and against the mark at 2.0084 shekels after 1.9986 on Wednesday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.3600 shekels.
